name: M.Sc. (Agriculture) Genetics and Plant Breeding
duration_note: University regulations based on the ICAR framework commonly allow up to 5 academic years (10 semesters) to complete the degree; the exact maximum is set by each university.

hero.summary: A two-year master's degree on the genetics behind crop traits and the methods used to develop improved varieties. Coursework spans classical, cytological, quantitative and molecular genetics alongside breeding methods, and every student completes a supervised research thesis, usually on breeding populations or germplasm.

overview.heading: Studying genetics and plant breeding at master's level
paragraphs: Genetics and Plant Breeding (often shortened to GPB) is the discipline behind new crop varieties and hybrids. It explains how traits such as yield, quality and resistance to pests, diseases or drought are inherited, and uses that knowledge to select and combine better plant types. In India, the M.Sc. is offered by state agricultural universities, ICAR deemed universities, central agricultural universities and private universities that follow the ICAR syllabus.

ICAR's restructured postgraduate framework requires 70 credits for a master's degree: 20 major, 8 minor, 6 supporting, 5 common, a 1-credit seminar and 30 credits of thesis research. Compulsory major courses in published GPB syllabi include principles of genetics, cytogenetics, plant breeding and quantitative genetics, along with cell biology and molecular genetics and biotechnology for crop improvement.

Electives typically cover mutation and heterosis breeding, breeding for stress resistance and quality, crop-group breeding, maintenance breeding and seed production, and plant genetic resources. The exact list and course codes depend on the university.

highlights.label: Typical entry degree
highlights.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture or an accepted allied four-year degree

highlights.label: National entrance
highlights.value: ICAR AIEEA (PG), conducted by NTA, Plant Sciences subject group

highlights.label: Next step
highlights.value: Ph.D. Genetics and Plant Breeding or a related plant science

who_should_apply: Agriculture graduates who liked genetics, cytology and crop improvement courses at undergraduate level
Students patient enough for season-long work making crosses, raising generations and scoring plants
Applicants curious about molecular markers, biotechnology and how they speed up variety development
Those aiming for careers in seed companies, breeding programmes or crop research institutes
Learners comfortable with the statistics used to estimate heritability and genetic variance

curriculum.heading: Course structure under the ICAR framework
curriculum.intro: Students take compulsory and elective GPB courses, a minor from a related plant science, supporting statistics or biotechnology courses, common research-skills courses and a thesis. The titles below come from published university syllabi aligned with ICAR BSMA; subject names, codes and electives vary by university.

structure.focus: Compulsory foundations in inheritance, chromosomes, breeding methods and molecular tools.
Electives on specific breeding approaches, crop groups and genetic resources.
courses: Breeding for Biotic and Abiotic Stress Resistance
Breeding Legumes, Oilseeds and Fibre Crops
Maintenance Breeding, Concepts of Variety Release and Seed Production

structure.focus: Allied subjects such as plant physiology, seed science, biotechnology or plant pathology, plus statistics.
courses: Minor courses from a related department chosen with the advisory committee

structure.focus: Research-skills courses shared by all master's students, a seminar and thesis research.
courses: Intellectual Property and its Management in Agriculture
Agricultural Research, Research Ethics and Rural Development Programmes

practical_learning.name: Thesis research
practical_learning.description: Students work on a breeding or genetics problem, such as evaluating germplasm, studying inheritance of a trait or testing hybrids, and defend a thesis at the end.

practical_learning.name: Field and laboratory practicals
practical_learning.description: Practical sessions cover emasculation and crossing, maintaining breeding records, chromosome preparation and basic molecular techniques.

practical_learning.name: Master's seminar
practical_learning.description: A one-credit seminar reviewing recent research on a chosen topic in crop improvement.

points: A four-year bachelor's degree in agriculture, typically B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; the ICAR bulletin and some universities also accept certain allied degrees for this subject, so check the subject-wise eligibility list for the admission year.
A minimum overall grade point average or percentage in the bachelor's degree, with relaxation for reserved categories, as set in the ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and each university's prospectus.
Requirements on the recognition or accreditation of the bachelor's degree vary; confirm them in the current bulletin.
Final-year students can usually apply but must complete the degree by the date the admitting university specifies.

routes.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
routes.description: National entrance test by NTA for ICAR. Genetics and Plant Breeding is one of the subjects under the Plant Sciences major subject group. The merit list is used for ICAR all-India quota seats and ICAR PG scholarships.

routes.name: State agricultural university entrance or merit
routes.description: Remaining seats in state agricultural universities are filled through state or university entrance tests, interviews or merit lists, which differ by state.

routes.name: Private and other universities
routes.description: Private universities following the ICAR syllabus generally hold their own entrance or merit-based admissions.

exams.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
exams.note: Candidates appear in the Plant Sciences subject group. Secondary reports describe a 120-question, 2-hour computer-based test with negative marking; confirm in the current bulletin.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility
steps.text: Check the subject-wise eligibility annexure of the ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and target university prospectuses for Genetics and Plant Breeding.

steps.title: Apply for entrance tests
steps.text: Register for ICAR AIEEA (PG) in the Plant Sciences group and for any state or university tests you plan to take.

steps.title: Participate in counselling
steps.text: After results, register for ICAR or university counselling and list your preferred universities and subjects.

steps.title: Complete admission
steps.text: Attend document verification and pay fees at the allotted university within the notified schedule.

fees.summary: Fees differ sharply between state agricultural universities, ICAR deemed universities and private universities, and between ICAR quota, state quota and management or NRI seats where these exist. Hostel and examination charges are often extra. ICAR AIEEA (PG) qualifiers admitted on ICAR seats may receive an ICAR PG scholarship under that year's rules. Always check the admitting university's current fee notice.

careers.heading: Career directions in crop improvement
careers.intro: Plant breeding postgraduates are recruited by public breeding programmes, seed companies and biotechnology firms, and many go on to doctoral research. Public sector roles are filled through competitive examinations, so the degree provides eligibility rather than assured placement.

roles.title: Assistant breeder or breeding associate
roles.description: Manages nurseries, crossing blocks and yield trials within a seed company or public breeding programme.

roles.title: Research fellow in crop improvement projects
roles.description: Works on funded projects in ICAR institutes or universities, collecting phenotypic and genotypic data.

roles.title: Seed production and quality officer
roles.description: Supervises seed multiplication, maintains varietal purity and coordinates with certification agencies.

roles.title: Germplasm or genebank assistant
roles.description: Helps characterise, document and conserve plant genetic resources.

roles.title: Assistant professor or scientist (with further qualifications)
roles.description: Usually requires qualifying ASRB or UGC NET and, increasingly, a Ph.D.

public_sector_routes: ASRB Agricultural Research Service (ARS) examination for ICAR scientist posts
State public service commission agriculture officer recruitment
IBPS Agricultural Field Officer (Specialist Officer) recruitment
higher_study: Ph.D. in Seed Science and Technology, Plant Biotechnology or Plant Genetic Resources where eligibility allows

skills: Planning crosses, managing segregating generations and keeping breeding records
Estimating genetic parameters such as variance, heritability and combining ability
Basic cytogenetic and molecular laboratory techniques
Designing and analysing multi-location varietal trials

faqs.question: Who can apply for M.Sc. Genetics and Plant Breeding?
faqs.answer: Mainly B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture graduates, with some allied degrees accepted by certain universities and in the ICAR bulletin. A minimum grade point average applies; check the subject-wise eligibility for the admission year.

faqs.question: Which ICAR AIEEA (PG) subject group covers this course?
faqs.answer: Genetics and Plant Breeding falls under the Plant Sciences major subject group of ICAR AIEEA (PG).

faqs.question: What are the core subjects?
faqs.answer: Published BSMA-based syllabi list principles of genetics, cytogenetics, plant breeding and quantitative genetics, together with cell biology and molecular genetics and biotechnology for crop improvement, as compulsory courses.

faqs.question: How much of the degree is research?
faqs.answer: In ICAR's restructured framework, thesis research carries 30 of the 70 credits, and the student must submit and defend a thesis.

faqs.question: Is this course only about molecular biology?
faqs.answer: No. Molecular tools are part of the syllabus, but much of the work involves field breeding: making crosses, evaluating populations and running trials over crop seasons.

faqs.question: What can I do after the M.Sc.?
faqs.answer: Options include breeding and seed roles in industry, research project posts, competitive exams such as ASRB NET or ARS, and a Ph.D. through ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF or university entrance.
